name: Debug Failing Audit (test-audit-loop)
description: LLM-classified failure handler for failed test_audit_report impulses (OpenSpec 2026-05-18-test-audit-loop §D). Subscribes to lifecycle:execution:succeeded filtered by output_shapes ∋ 'test_audit_report' AND passed === false. Three tasks: (1) classify_failure — LLM resolver categorises the failure into one of {audit_insensitive, audit_noisy, audit_misaligned, audit_record_incomplete}; (2) propose_modification — LLM resolver produces a structured code_modification_proposal { target_file, diff, risk_tier, risk_assessment ∈ {low,medium,high}, rationale }; (3) route_proposal — deterministic routing: risk_tier='test_only' (path confined to validation/scripts/) emits a code_modification_proposal for the auto-merge lane; any path outside validation/scripts/ emits a system_modification_proposal; low verification_confidence falls through to the standard HumanResolver tier via human_review_request — NOT a new audit-specific escalation surface (spec Requirement R4). The proposal carries supersedes: [...] of prior unmerged proposals for the same test, plus a lifecycle dedupe key of (test_registration_id, audit_subtype) so concurrent dispatches collapse to one proposal.

variables.name: lifecycle
variables.description: Set by the lifecycle dispatcher to the execution:succeeded payload. Carries executionId of the audit producing the failed test_audit_report plus parentDepth/composition_chain for the depth-2 recursion cap (audits of audits cap at depth 2, same as audit-test-report). debug-failing-audit itself does not invoke audit-test-report so the cap is inherited rather than re-checked here.

variables.name: test_audit_report_id
variables.description: Impulse id of the failing test_audit_report. Derived from lifecycle.output_impulse_ids when invoked via subscription; pass explicitly for ad-hoc/workbench dispatches.

variables.name: verification_threshold
variables.description: verification_confidence below this routes through human_review_request (HumanResolver tier). Spec Requirement R4: this is the SAME gate any other activity uses — no audit-specific human-escalation surface.

variables.name: debugLLMModel
variables.description: Model used by classify_failure + propose_modification. Sonnet-tier (vs Haiku for audit-test-report) because proposing a code modification needs deeper reasoning about the failure mode.

tasks.description: Fetch the failing test_audit_report. The downstream classifier needs the validation_results[] (which check failed), the failed_evidence.audit_subtype (classifier seed), and the originating test_registration_id + test_report_id (so propose_modification can target the right file).
tasks.notes: The test_audit_report shape (Phase A) supports filtering by test_registration_id, test_report_id, and passed. id-level lookup is done via the _filter side-channel that the resolver narrows post-fetch when needed. When the lookup returns zero rows the downstream tasks short-circuit via the standard 'empty input impulse' propagation.

tasks.description: LLM classifier: read the failed test_audit_report and confirm or refine its failed_evidence.audit_subtype. The audit's deterministic checks already proposed a subtype (record_incomplete > insensitive > noisy > misaligned per the compose_audit_report priority); the LLM either confirms or upgrades based on the validation_results details. Emits a validation_result impulse with failure_mode = verifier_negative carrying the final audit_subtype.
tasks.notes: The audit_subtype lives inside failed_evidence per spec §F — the top-level failure_mode.type remains 'verifier_negative'. The closed five-type enumeration in validators-and-failure-modes/failure-mode-taxonomy/spec.md is preserved.

tasks.description: LLM proposes a concrete code modification: target_file, unified diff, and risk_assessment ∈ {low, medium, high}. The audit_subtype drives the proposal shape: insensitive → tighten the test assertion to read more deeply (typically a trace-id or impulse-id reference); noisy → reduce variance (deterministic seed, tighter input bounds); misaligned → rewrite the discrimination_claim or refactor the test; record_incomplete → add the missing decision-record fields. risk_tier is derived deterministically by route_proposal from the target_file path; the LLM only proposes the diff + risk_assessment.

prompt.template:
You are proposing a code modification for a failing test audit.

Classification (JSON): {{impulse:classify_failure_result}}
Failed audit report (JSON): {{impulse:fetch_audit_report_result}}

Propose ONE concrete modification. Default target is the test file itself (validation/scripts/<test_id>.ts when test_id is a validation script). Only target system code (outside validation/scripts/) when the failure is clearly an under-instrumented system path (rare).

Audit-subtype-specific guidance:
- audit_record_incomplete: add the missing decision-record references — every assertion should cite an impulse id or trace event.
- audit_insensitive: tighten assertions so the perturbation actually flips the outcome (e.g. check a specific tool-call argument, not just goal completion).
- audit_noisy: pin nondeterministic inputs (seeds, time, random sampling). Document the noise source in the rationale.
- audit_misaligned: rewrite the discrimination_claim or refactor the test so the claim and the test actually match.

Emit EXACTLY this JSON object:
{
  "target_file": "<path, absolute or repo-relative>",
  "diff": "<unified-diff string>",
  "risk_assessment": "low|medium|high",
  "rationale": "<2-3 sentences explaining what changes and why>",
  "verification_confidence": <0..1>
}

tasks.notes: risk_assessment is independent of risk_tier — assessment is the LLM's confidence in the change correctness; risk_tier is computed by route_proposal from the target_file path. A 'low' risk_assessment on a system-code modification still becomes a system_modification_proposal (not auto-mergeable) because the file path is outside validation/scripts/. The verification_confidence field gates the human_review_request branch (spec Requirement R4); when below verification_threshold the proposal routes to HumanResolver.

tasks.description: Deterministic routing per spec §D and Requirement R4. Reads the LLM's proposal + verification_confidence; the SAME verification_confidence < threshold gate any other activity uses routes to human_review_request, otherwise the proposal emits as code_modification_proposal (risk_tier='test_only' when target_file lives under validation/scripts/) or system_modification_proposal (target_file outside validation/scripts/). Carries supersedes: [...] of any prior unmerged proposals for the same (test_registration_id, audit_subtype) so auto-merge picks the newest non-superseded entry.
tasks.notes:
Three branches per spec Requirement R4:
  1. verification_confidence < verification_threshold → emit human_review_request (HumanResolver tier — the standard low-confidence gate, NOT an audit-specific escalation). The proposal is still persisted via code_modification_proposal_write so the human reviewer has a concrete artifact, but the routing impulse on the wire is human_review_request.
  2. target_file starts with 'validation/scripts/' → risk_tier='test_only', emit code_modification_proposal (auto-merge lane per design.md §D.3).
  3. otherwise → risk_tier mirrors risk_assessment (low/medium/high), emit system_modification_proposal.

The _routing block is read by the dispatcher to determine which output shape to surface; the underlying write always goes to code_modification_proposal_write so the proposal persists regardless of routing.

The supersedes array is computed by a read-side query against prior code_modification_proposal rows matching (test_registration_id, classification) — the deduplication is at PROPOSAL level (carry forward unmerged predecessors) rather than at DISPATCH level (which is handled by the subscription dedupe_key). spec §H concurrency contract: concurrent dispatches with the same dedupe_key collapse to one proposal at the subscription layer; supersedes covers sequentially-emitted proposals across multiple audit cycles.

metadata.author: test-audit-loop
metadata.subscriberContract: subscription.shape = 'lifecycle:execution:succeeded' with filter output_shapes_contains = 'test_audit_report' AND passed === false. dedupe_key = '{test_registration_id}:{audit_subtype}' — concurrent dispatches (e.g. weekly probe + ad-hoc audit) collapse to ONE proposal per (test, subtype) per dispatch window per spec §H.
metadata.outputContract: Emits EXACTLY ONE of three shapes per dispatch (spec Requirement R4): code_modification_proposal (test_only or low/medium/high risk, when verification_confidence ≥ threshold), system_modification_proposal (target outside validation/scripts/, when confidence ≥ threshold), or human_review_request (when confidence < threshold). The human_review_request branch routes through the standard HumanResolver tier — NOT a new audit-specific escalation path.
metadata.auditSubtypeContract: classify_failure refines the audit_subtype within failed_evidence (verifier_negative subtype), never introducing a new top-level failure_mode.type. The closed five-type enumeration is preserved (spec §F).
metadata.recursionCap: debug-failing-audit does not invoke audit-test-report directly, so the depth-2 cap is enforced upstream in audit-test-report's compose_audit_report task. Meta-audits of meta-audits (depth 3+) are rejected with safety_breach at the audit-test-report dispatch, never reaching this template.
